system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
*The Seller labels several positions “[STANDARD]”, but that label does not make them agreed or acceptable. Recommendations below are from Wattlebridge’s perspective, against the AUD 24 million debt-free/cash-free deal baseline.*

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | A higher cap that reflects potential exposure and the value of the warranties; separate, higher caps for specific risks where warranted. | **Reject as drafted; seek a materially higher general cap.** AUD 4.8m may be inadequate to address aggregate warranty losses. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and basket, preferably a tipping basket so recovery starts at the threshold once crossed. | **Negotiate down both thresholds and make the basket tipping.** The proposed thresholds may exclude meaningful claims and leave the Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months; Seller proposes applying any limitation to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties and clear, separate periods for tax, fundamental, title and indemnity claims, with no blanket extension of the general limit. | **Reject the blanket rule; specify each category and its own survival period.** Otherwise the general deadline could unintentionally cut off claims that need longer to emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits. | Fundamental and title claims outside the general cap and with longer survival, subject to an appropriate separate cap (potentially the price) and applicable law. | **Reject; carve fundamental/title claims out of the general regime.** Defects in the Seller’s authority or ownership go to the basis of the acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out stated. | Expressly exclude fraud (including fraudulent misrepresentation) from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to the fullest lawful extent. | **Require an express fraud carve-out.** The Seller should not obtain contractual protection for its own fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room as at 22 September 2026, Accounts, statutory registers and public corporate records; Seller disclaims admissions of breach or required action. | Specific, fair disclosure against each relevant warranty, with precise document references; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure and require specific disclosure.** A broad incorporation-by-reference approach makes it difficult to know what qualifies the warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No general imputation of adviser or constructive knowledge; if any qualifier is accepted, limit it to actual knowledge of named deal personnel after defined enquiry and only for specifically disclosed matters. | **Reject as drafted.** “Discoverable” knowledge would shift diligence risk to Buyer and undermine the warranties. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller to use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty’s written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of conditions are absent. | A condition to Completion requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction/waiver of all associated conditions; termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make valid consent and condition satisfaction a Completion condition.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and consent alone may not satisfy clause 11.3. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | About AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. | Repayment at or before Completion from Seller funds or completion monies, with lender payout evidence and effective release/discharge of all security as a Completion deliverable. | **Do not accept a post-Completion release.** The debt-free/cash-free baseline and security exposure require discharge at Completion, not a promise to procure it later. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional Completion bonuses are “for the Seller” and omitted from funds flow. Disclosure notes payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unspecified. | Quantify and fund the bonuses and all on-costs in the completion accounts/funds flow, with clear allocation and no leakage to Buyer. | **Require an agreed, fully costed funds-flow treatment before signing/Completion.** The omitted bonuses and uncertain on-costs could otherwise reduce value or create post-Completion liabilities. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller says it is adequate. DD-004/010 show transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; AUD 180,000 remains open, without independent non-payment verification or assignment confirmation. | A specific indemnity and Completion deliverables covering payment, valid assignment/transfer of all Project Materials and any resulting loss, with payment evidence and confirmatory assignment. | **Expand the indemnity and make verified payment and transfer a Completion condition.** The current narrow indemnity does not ensure the Buyer receives the IP it is acquiring. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | DD-006 described as preliminary and not expected to be material; no specific remedy offered. Disclosure records a link sent to an unintended address and possible exposure of about 1,240 records, with access and notification status unknown. | Full investigation and remediation, required notifications, evidence and cooperation; specific warranty/indemnity for incident-related liabilities and costs, with appropriate survival and cap treatment. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not presumed immaterial.** The record does not establish access, scope or notification duties, so obtain facts and contractual protection before Completion. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 described as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure says they are related and does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course. | Review both DD-008 and DD-011 together; confirm scope, terms, termination rights, accrual and ordinary-course status, and reflect any unusual commitments in the warranties, debt-like items or price mechanics. | **Require clarification and assess the aggregate exposure before accepting the characterization.** The disclosure does not support treating the renewals as ordinary or unavoidable. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; general time limits apply unless expressly stated otherwise; tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, fraud and other claims, expressly stating which caps, thresholds, time limits and remedies apply to each. | **Reject an all-Claims regime and negotiate an express category matrix.** Without clear separation, general limitations may inadvertently swallow negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on the share register at DD-012 as evidence that it holds 100% of issued shares. | Verify the register against the constitution, ASIC records and executed share/issue history; obtain title, encumbrance and authority warranties and valid transfer documents. | **Treat DD-012 as a source, not conclusive verification.** The register alone does not establish an unbroken, unencumbered chain of title or proper transfer authority. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime, but no specific terms are provided here. | Review the actual SPA drafting and negotiate robust tax and IP warranties, appropriate survival/caps and specific indemnities for identified exposures; do not assume agreement from this summary. | **Keep these terms open pending clause-level review.** The Seller’s assertion that they are settled does not identify or establish the protections the Buyer needs. |
=== END ADVICE ===
